title: Trade and Cargo Academy
description: The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Charleston District (SAC) has a new requirement for construction of a Trade and Cargo Academy at the Federal Law Enforcement Training Center (FLETC). The requirement will include hazardous material abatement and selective demolition of the current vacant 30,000 SF, three-story building, while preserving the existing main lobby and ensuring uninterrupted utility service to the occupied east wing. In its place, a new 28,400 SF, two-story, flood-resilient facility will be constructed. Due to poor soil quality and its location within FEMA Zone AE, the TCA will use a deep precast concrete pile foundation with pile-supported slabs, a heavy-duty steel frame to withstand high wind/seismic demands, a modern rainscreen envelope, and fully integrated building systems (HVAC, LED lighting, and security infrastructure). The interior will have space for instructional use on the first floor (including classrooms, an auditorium, and production spaces) and administrative open offices on the second floor. FLETC also has a requirement for the construction of a new Cargo Security and Seized Property Training Facility (CSSPTF), a separate one-story 5,985 SF facility purpose-built to support U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) training. Specifically designed for hands-on vehicle/cargo inspection, evidence processing, and simulated seized property storage, this site-adapted facility will also be elevated on a deep pile foundation to comply with stringent floodplain requirements. A key engineering focus for this site is the implementation of pile-supported stormwater piping under paved areas to mitigate soil settlement risks. Both facilities are engineered for a minimum 40-year operational lifespan, integrating highly durable, low-maintenance coastal materials, and will comply fully with the latest federal energy conservation standards, DHS security criteria, and 2021 building codes. These facilities are essential for the increased student enrollment and additional courses offered supporting FLETC Charleston.

The manometry probe (or catheter) required to operate the HRM system is a thin, flexible tube equipped with sensors, inserted through the nose or mouth into the gastrointestinal tract to measure muscle pressure and coordination. This new request is for a one-time firm-fixed-price contract to procure replacement manometry probes compatible with the HRM system that are at end of lifecycle. The supplies/services needed are: Manoscan ESO Z CATH X1 � Mfr. Part #: 3890 � Quantity of 4 Each HRM Catheter Extended WARRANTY 1 YEAR � Mfr. These catheters utilize proprietary connectors, hardware interfaces, and system recognition features that are unique to Medtronic equipment. The HRM system requires OEM-compatible manometry probes to avoid calibration drift, invalid pressure profiles, and adverse impact on clinical decisions. Probes from non?OEM sources are not validated with this system�s firmware and sterile pathway, creating risk to patient safety and data integrity. Medical device accessories must be assessed in context of the parent device; compatibility and risk controls apply. The project started in 1995, and the next data collection is planned for 2028. Donegal is a narrow masonry arch structure with a span of 1.83 m and a width of 5.28 m. The bridge and its immediate approaches have been identified as a safety blackspot due to a combination of poor horizontal and vertical alignment, substandard cross-sectional width, and deteriorating pavement conditions. The western approach exhibits fatigue and alligator cracking, while the bridge itself has suffered parapet damage from vehicular impacts, compromising edge restraint and posing a significant hazard to road users. The purpose of this contract is to conduct the detailed ground investigation to progress the detailed design of the scheme. The GI will extend over the entire length of the proposed road development. Ground Investigation points will be carried out in the areas of the existing and new road construction with a number of trial pits to be carried out in green field sites. Secured Zone Access: Once the temporary security fencing is approved and accepted by the Contracting Officer�s Representative (COR), no escort shall be required within the active secured work zone during construction, allowing the contractor to work within the secured boundary unimpeded.
